summary: This bill imposes a 100% tax on any payments received by a former U.S. president, their family, or controlled entities from settlement funds tied to civil lawsuits against the federal government, requires fund administrators to report such payments publicly, and adds penalties for nonpayment or failure to report.

scores.thoughts: The bill imposes a tax on certain settlement payments but does not authorize, appropriate, or alter any government expenditures. It has no direct or indirect effect on spending levels.

The core of the bill is the creation of a new Chapter 50B in the Internal Revenue Code that levies a 100% tax on specified settlement fund payments received by former presidents, their families, or controlled entities. It also adds penalties for non-payment and reporting requirements. This is a clear, targeted increase in taxation on high-income individuals.
